title: Shape-invariant split-K NF4 down-projection experiment
status: B1-correct in finite development pilots; no-go as current end-to-end performance candidate

operator_screen.target: Qwen2.5-3B NF4 down_proj 11008x2048, N=16, K=256, num_warps=1

whole_model_pilots.baseline_comparison: Earlier warp1-only pilot summary on the same three prompts measured 1.14228x versus B1 and 0.91600x versus BNB. This is a cross-run diagnostic comparison, not a paired A/B estimate; currently available evidence favors retaining warp1-only as the better schedule.

paired_same_process_comparison.protocol: 3 prompts x 3 alternating-order repeats; same loaded model/process; B1 block generation only; 32 output tokens; K=1/R=2/padded attention
paired_same_process_comparison.interpretation: Split8 is 3.8% slower end-to-end than warp1 in this direct paired comparison, despite faster down_proj operator timings. The prompt-level interval treats prompts as the independent units; the repeat-level interval is diagnostic because repeats share prompts.

workspace_reuse.decision: Reusing the split partial buffer did not remove the end-to-end slowdown.

warp_count.decision: One warp remains the fastest split8 configuration; more warps do not rescue the method.

decision: Retain split8 only as an opt-in research prototype with its own contract. Direct paired end-to-end evidence rejects it as the selected performance schedule. Workspace reuse and warp-count sweeps did not improve it. Stop this split-K branch and prioritize a materially different dataflow. Do not run held-out evaluation.
limitations: Finite evidence on one GPU, one model revision, one K/row-count, and three development prompts.
Zero observed mismatch does not prove all-input equivalence.
The split-K arithmetic schedule is a separate B1 reference and is not equivalent to original BNB by construction.
